title: OpenAI Responses API and SDK Workflows
summary: This intermediate module enables you to plan and evaluate a basic workflow that sends input through the OpenAI Responses API, inspects the returned response, and decides whether to continue or stop. After completing it, you can distinguish the API interaction from the SDK layer and identify the checks required at each workflow stage.
objectives: Describe the roles of the Responses API and an SDK in the same workflow.
Plan a workflow that prepares input, sends a request, inspects the response, and determines the next action.
Check returned output before using it in an application or a later request.
Explain which source citation changed in this update and what the correction affected.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that you understand the basic idea of an authenticated API request and can read structured response data. It does not assume knowledge of a particular programming language, SDK implementation, version, configuration key, or deployment environment.

The goal is to understand the workflow rather than memorize implementation-specific syntax. You will learn where input preparation, request submission, response inspection, and continuation decisions belong.

sections.title: API and SDK roles
paragraphs: The Responses API defines the interaction in which an application supplies input and receives a response from OpenAI. An SDK provides a client-library layer through which application code can perform that interaction.

These layers are related but not identical. The API determines the request and response behavior. The SDK provides programming-language-oriented ways to construct the request, send it, and access the returned data. Keeping the distinction clear helps you reason about whether a problem belongs to the API interaction, the client-library layer, or the surrounding application.

sections.title: A reusable workflow
paragraphs: First, define the result the application needs and prepare input that communicates that task. Include the relevant context, constraints, and requested output form. Do not add unrelated context merely because it is available.

Second, send the prepared input through the Responses API, directly or through an SDK. The surrounding application remains responsible for deciding when to make the request and what information to provide.

Third, inspect the returned response before using it. Confirm that the response is present, identify the generated output needed by the application, and check whether that output satisfies the task and required form.

Fourth, decide whether to stop, revise the input, or continue the interaction. A workflow should not treat every returned output as automatically suitable for display, storage, or use in another operation.
sections.callout: A successful request does not by itself establish that the generated output is accurate, relevant, safe, or suitable for the application's purpose.

sections.title: State and application responsibility
paragraphs: If an interaction continues across requests, the application must deliberately manage the context needed for the next step using behavior supported by the Responses API. The exact implementation depends on the selected SDK and application design, which this module does not specify.

Keep API output separate from trusted application data until it has passed the checks required by the use case. The application, not the generated response, determines whether an operation is permitted and whether the result is ready for further use.

sections.title: Source correction in this update
paragraphs: The changed citation was the prior entry that pointed to content/modules/openai-practice/openai-responses-api-and-sdk-workflows.json, the module file itself. That entry had an unregistered publisher and had never been verified.

This update replaces that self-citation with the official OpenAI Responses API reference over HTTPS. The change affects source provenance, verification metadata, and the next review date. The instructional workflow remains otherwise unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Responses API from an SDK?
choices: The API defines the request and response interaction, while an SDK provides a client-library layer for performing that interaction.
The SDK defines OpenAI's service behavior, while the API only formats text for display.
The API and SDK are unrelated systems that cannot be used in the same workflow.
The SDK determines whether generated output is accurate.
questions.explanation: The module explains that the API defines the interaction and that an SDK provides a programming-language-oriented client layer for carrying it out.

questions.prompt: What should an application do immediately after receiving a response?
choices: Automatically treat every output as approved for any use.
Inspect the response and check whether its output satisfies the task and required form.
Discard the response without reading it.
Assume the SDK has verified every factual statement.
questions.explanation: The workflow requires inspecting the returned response and checking that the needed output satisfies the task before the application uses it.

questions.prompt: After inspecting generated output, what decision belongs to the application?
choices: Whether to stop, revise the input, or continue the interaction.
Whether to redefine the Responses API for every request.
Whether to accept the output without any use-case checks.
Whether to conceal the output from the application.
questions.explanation: The final workflow stage is an application decision to stop, revise the input, or continue based on the inspected result.

questions.prompt: What did the source correction in this update affect?
choices: It introduced a new SDK version and new configuration keys.
It replaced an unverified self-citation with the official API reference and updated verification metadata.
It changed the module from intermediate to beginner.
questions.explanation: The update replaces the module's self-citation with the official OpenAI Responses API reference. It affects provenance and verification metadata, not the instructional workflow.
